thread:
Zoe H.: hi all, day 1 question — i'm on Fedora 36 using WireGuard (split-tunnel) that the onboarding script set up. I can ssh to the bastion by IP but anything like `curl http://vault.internal/health` fails with DNS. ping by IP works. anyone seen wireguard + split-tunnel DNS oddness?
Kyle (infra): welcome Zoe! yep, WG often doesn't push DNS by default. What does `resolvectl status` show for wg0?
Zoe H.: `resolvectl status` shows only my home resolver on wlan0, wg0 up but no DNS. i tried adding `10.14.4.8 vault.internal` to /etc/hosts and curl works, but `git clone git.internal:repo.git` still fails (timeout).
Priya (devex): git via SSH often needs ProxyJump rather than hosts. You can add to `~/.ssh/config`:
```
Host git.internal
  HostName git.internal
  ProxyJump zoe@bastion.redwood.internal
```
Then `git clone git.internal:repo.git` should go through bastion.
Zoe H.: added ProxyJump, clone works! thanks. quick follow-up: i'd rather not keep /etc/hosts forever — what's the recommended BYOD-safe approach so i don't need to port-forward for tools?
Kyle (infra): two options we use for BYOD: 1) have the WireGuard client set DNS in the wg config (add `DNS = 10.12.2.2` under the interface for resolvconf/systemd-resolved to pick up), or 2) use a small systemd-resolved config to route only the internal domain to the corp resolver. if you're ok editing wg conf, we can push a one-line change to your onboarding config.
Zoe H.: i'd prefer not to edit wg config if it means replacing the onboarding file frequently. what's the systemd-resolved route option?
Kyle (infra): create `/etc/systemd/resolved.conf.d/internal.conf` with:
```
[Resolve]
DNS=10.12.2.2
Domains=~internal.redwood
```
Then `sudo systemctl restart systemd-resolved`. That tells systemd-resolved to send queries for `*.internal` to the corporate DNS and leaves your other DNS alone. Works nicely with split-tunnel.
Zoe H.: i tried that but got `Permission denied` when editing — forgot sudo. applied it and restarted resolved, now `resolvectl status` shows the internal DNS for `internal.redwood` and `curl vault.internal` works. awesome.
Priya (devex): heads up for docker: if Docker daemon is running as a service it might use the old resolv.conf, restart docker with `sudo systemctl restart docker` to pick up new DNS.
Zoe H.: restarted docker, but `docker login registry.internal:5000` still times out. any ideas?
Kyle (infra): registry sits on a different subnet that only accepts connections from inside the VPC or via the bastion. simplest onboarding unblock is SSH local forward from your host: `ssh -L 5500:registry.internal:5000 zoe@bastion.redwood.internal -N` then `docker login localhost:5500`. we can also temporarily whitelist your public IP for direct registry access if you'd rather.
IT Support Bot: (automated) To request whitelist, reply `@IT Support Bot whitelist` and include your public IP.
Zoe H.: ok i'll do the forward for now. ran the ssh -L and docker login to localhost:5500 worked. deploy-bot showed session open.
deploy-bot: (system) bastion session for zoe started, audit id: e7b2c
Zoe H.: big thanks — this unblocked onboarding. Kyle, can you file a follow-up to add the internal DNS route to the WireGuard onboarding template so future BYOD hires have it?
Kyle (infra): done, opened INF-4399 to add `Domains=~internal.redwood` to the resolved conf in the onboarding script and to document the docker/registry caveat. i'll keep the ticket pinned to onboarding docs.
Priya (devex): welcome again Zoe! if you want i can hop on a quick call to pair on tidying up the local changes so nothing persists after offboarding.
Zoe H.: would love that, thanks everyone! :raised_hands:
